newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures settled higher after a weak start but remained vulnerable, like their U.S. and German counterparts, ahead of Friday U.S. payroll data preceded by U.S. producer price and German jobless data on Thursday.
"The U.S. market is looking poorly which is a worry," said one trader.

The March bond future contract finished MATIF trading 0.16 points higher at 128.02 after a low of 127.60 shortly after the open, while the March PIBOR interest rate future settled two points up at 96.71, shy of a new contract high of 96.73.
PIBOR resilience was attributed by several traders to some large non-resident buys.
French futures fared relatively better than their German counterparts after some traders earlier cited investors selling Germany and buying France.

Earlier the Berlin-based DIW economic research institute revised its 1997 growth forecast for Germany down to two percent from 2.5 percent. German unemployment data due on Thursday could further focus minds on Bonn's deficit reduction capacity.
Analysts are looking for a seasonally adjuested rise of 35,000 to 60,000 in December from November's record 4.1 million.
In the cash market, the 10-year yield spread over Germany moved to minus seven from minus 8 after earlier moving to as far as minus 10.

Economists polled recently by Reuters forecast, on average, U.S. December payrolls growth of 192,000, an unemployment rate of 5.30 percent and a 0.2 percent rise in hourly earnings in data to be released at 1330 GMT on Friday.
On average they forecast overall December producer price data due on Thursday to show a 0.3 percent rise and a 0.1 percent rise excluding energy and food prices.
